Q: What is this: [Ljava.lang.Object;? A: 
// Source - https://stackoverflow.com/a/65028897
// Posted by chill appreciator
// Retrieved 2026-03-03, License - CC BY-SA 4.0

SELECT COUNT(i.relname)
FROM
    pg_class t,
    pg_class i,
    pg_index ix
WHERE
    t.oid = ix.indrelid
    and i.oid = ix.indexrelid
    and t.relkind = 'r'
    and t.relname = 'tableName'
    and i.relname = 'indexName';

Q: Powershell' is not recognized as an internal or external command, operable program or batch file A:

Old question, but I had this issue today.

I wrote a batch script that subsequently executes a Powershell script, and accidentally used %path% as a local variable, to store the path of some unrelated file, in the batch script.

However, using %path% as a local variable will quietly override your (very important) environment %PATH% variable, which happens to include the path to powershell.exe.

Thankfully, this change is not permanent (unless you used setx in the batch file).

Q: Gitbook link to a tab A:

GitBook automatically generates unique URLs for each tabbed section within a page, allowing you to link directly to a specific tab.

You can retrieve these links in two ways:

  • Direct URL: Simply navigate to the desired tab and copy the URL from your browser’s address bar (e.g., the #docker-deployment or #amazon-eks-deployment anchors in the PDC documentation).
    https://docs.pentaho.com/pdc-admin/ldc-advanced-configuration-ut_cp#docker-deployment
    https://docs.pentaho.com/pdc-admin/ldc-advanced-configuration-ut_cp#amazon-eks-deployment

  • Internal Cross-Referencing: When adding a cross-reference, use the #Link option in the editor. GitBook will prompt you to select the specific tab or section.

Q: Given a start and end datetime, generate a row index for each 12 hour shift spanned A:

Asked and answered, but a join might be much faster and gives you another option. Base R apart from the range join.

# character to datetime 
x$start <- as.POSIXct(x$start)
x$end <- as.POSIXct(x$end)

# 12-hour shift calendar
shift_start <- seq(
  from = as.POSIXct(paste(as.Date(min(x$start)), "06:00:00")),
  to   = as.POSIXct(paste(as.Date(max(x$end)),   "18:00:00")),
  by   = "12 hours"
)

# shift starts spanned
spanned <- fjoin::fjoin_inner(x, data.frame(shift_start),
                              on=c("start < shift_start", "end > shift_start"))

# stack and sort
x$shift_start <- x$start
y <- rbind(x, spanned)
y <- y[order(y$id, y$shift_start),]

#>   id               start                 end         shift_start
#> 1  A 2026-02-01 15:30:00 2026-02-02 09:30:00 2026-02-01 15:30:00
#> 3  A 2026-02-01 15:30:00 2026-02-02 09:30:00 2026-02-01 18:00:00
#> 4  A 2026-02-01 15:30:00 2026-02-02 09:30:00 2026-02-02 06:00:00
#> 2  B 2026-02-05 19:00:00 2026-02-06 20:00:00 2026-02-05 19:00:00
#> 5  B 2026-02-05 19:00:00 2026-02-06 20:00:00 2026-02-06 06:00:00
#> 6  B 2026-02-05 19:00:00 2026-02-06 20:00:00 2026-02-06 18:00:00

Edit: alternative version is overlap join then pmax, pmin (instead of range join then rbind)

shift_start <- seq(
  from = as.POSIXct(paste(as.Date(min(x$start)-1), "06:00:00")),
  to   = as.POSIXct(paste(as.Date(max(x$end)+1),   "18:00:00")),
  by   = "12 hours"
)
y <- fjoin::fjoin_inner(
  x,
  data.frame(shift_start, shift_end=shift_start + 12*60*60),
  on=c("start < shift_end", "end > shift_start")) # overlap join condition
y <- data.frame(
  id = y$id,
  shift_start = pmax(y$start, y$shift_start),
  shift_end = pmin(y$end, y$shift_end)
)
